main_text.p: Quod sit exhibitum: Ratio una: Tempus exhibitionis a Deo destinatum, & oraculis prophetarum definitum praeteriit: Ergo necesse est fateantur Messiam venisse: aut vanitatis accusent Deum & prophetas. Antecedens probetur.

1. Gen. 49: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, donec veniat Silo. Sensus oraculi: Sub idem tempus concidet regnum Judaicum, & veniet Messias: qui dicitur שילה [?] h.e, Filius eius nempe, Judæ κατ' ἐξοχὴν [?].

Obiectio Judæorum, שילה [?] faciunt nomen urbis in tribu Ephraim Jud. 21. hoc sensu: Non veniet finis Siloh, donec Saul eligatur in regem in Siloh. Alii igitur de Saule, alii de Jeroboamo rege eligendo in Siloh dictum volunt. Alii etiam de Nebucadnezare misso ad delendum templum & urbem: quasi sit שילה [?] missus & mittendus, ut habet vetus latina:
1. quia in electione Saulis Juda nondum habuerat sceptrum:
2. per Jeroboamum sceptrum non est plane ablatum à Juda.

3. quia in captivitate, & postea mansit aliquod ἀξίωμα [?] sceptri in Juda, h.e. posteris Davidis: Duces: Sanhedrin magnum: etsi sine titulo regio: quem tamen resumsit Iohannes Hyrcanus filius Simonis Machabæi: iterum vero perdidit nepos ejus Hyrcanus ultimus ab Herode trucidatus.
4. Chaldæus Paraphrastes & veteres Thalmudistæ sic vertunt: Donec veniat Messias Rex: & expo-

page.notes: Greek and Hebrew words marked [?] are read from a small scan and may contain errors in individual letters. The line "Judæ κατ' ἐξοχὴν" and the Greek ἀξίωμα are the least certain. Printed "Iuda" and "Iudaicum" were changed to Juda and Judaicum for u/v and i/j spelling. The sign before "Antecedens" is a printer's mark and was left out. The final line is cut off at the foot by the page edge, and "expo-" is the printed hyphen.
